english: The ellipse $E:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{18}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}=1$ is a reflecting curve. A ray of light starting from the point $S(3,0)$ travels along the line joining $S$ to the point $B(0,3)$ and is reflected by $E$ at $B$. The reflected ray meets $E$ again at the point $Q$. The tangent to $E$ at $Q$ meets the $x$-axis at $(\alpha,0)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: दीर्घवृत्त $E:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{18}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}=1$ एक परावर्तक वक्र है। बिन्दु $S(3,0)$ से चलने वाली एक प्रकाश किरण $S$ को बिन्दु $B(0,3)$ से मिलाने वाली रेखा के अनुदिश चलती है तथा $B$ पर $E$ द्वारा परावर्तित होती है। परावर्तित किरण $E$ को पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। $Q$ पर $E$ की स्पर्श रेखा $x$-अक्ष को $(\alpha,0)$ पर मिलती है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Reflection property: a ray through one focus is reflected through the other, so the reflected ray is the line $BS'$: $y=x+3$
solution_full: For $E$: $a^{2}=18$, $b^{2}=9$, $a^{2}e^{2}=9$, so the foci are $S(3,0)$ and $S'(-3,0)$; $B(0,3)$ is an end of the minor axis, on $E$.

Reflection property: the normal at a point of the ellipse bisects the angle between the focal radii, so a ray coming from one focus is reflected towards the other focus. Hence the reflected ray at $B$ travels along $BS'$.
Check at $B$: the tangent at $B$ is $y=3$ and the normal is vertical; the incoming direction $(-3,3)$ reflects to $(-3,-3)$, which points from $B$ to $S'(-3,0)$.
originality_note: New: a light path from a focus via the end of the minor axis, where the reflection property sends the ray through the other focus to a second point whose tangent is then used (way 5). Closest known: rays from one focus reflect through the other focus. Different because: the property is a step inside a longer construction (second intersection, then the tangent there), not the answer itself.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked the reflection at B both by the focal property and by reflecting the direction vector in the normal, and that Q is the only other intersection. Changed: No change.
key_step: Reflection property sends the ray from S via B through S'(-3,0); intersect BS' with E to get Q(-4,-1).
justification: Two ideas linked (reflection property of the ellipse, then the tangent at the new point) in numerical format. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3), an ellipse question chaining tangent properties.

concept_use.Reflection property of Ellipse: The reflection property sends the ray from the focus S(3,0), reflected at B, through the other focus S'(-3,0); this gives the line y = x + 3 and the point Q(-4,-1).
concept_use.Tangent and normal for Ellipse: The tangent to E at Q, -4x/18 - y/9 = 1, meets the x-axis at alpha = -9/2.
